- Model consistently underestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after sharp spikes or volatility; adjust downward bias for first 5–7 days.
- Overshoots occur after large upward moves in history; cap forecast peaks at 10–15% above recent high for 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–14 day horizon; if forecast is >15% above 30d mean, reduce by 5–8% for next 7 days.
- Sentiment history is neutral (all 0.00) — no behavioral signal — so ignore sentiment-driven corrections unless sentiment shifts >0.30.
- If true outcome shows sudden drop after spike, model tends to lag — add 1–2 day lag correction for 10–15 day horizon.
- For 30d horizon, model often overfits recent low points — use 30d moving average as baseline, then apply 5–10% upward adjustment if recent 7d mean > 30d mean.
